criteria.text: **Why the existing staleness state did not fire**, reproduced: show the two historical entries (or faithful copies under the OS temp root) rendering without a staleness signal before the change, and with one after. Explain the 182-versus-183 annotation inconsistency with the code path that produced each.
**Which parts are enforced mechanically and which rest on wording.** For anything that rests on ship.md wording, say what would catch it if the wording were ignored.
**That a live entry is not falsely flagged**: an entry referencing a running task, and an entry referencing no task at all, both render without staleness noise. Show it.

**`npm run build`, `npm run test`, and `npm run lint` end green after the last write**, each with its direct exit code and totals. Establish the pre-change baseline yourself with both dependency trees installed as real directories; the recorded setup baseline may show `.tsx` spec failures that are a dependency-layout artifact, documented in `docs/orchestration_contract/final_verification.md` — read it rather than treating those as pre-existing defects.
**Say what each supplied quantity in this brief depends on that the brief did not state**, and whether that changes what it is worth.

**Re-read the run's declared reality checks before the terminal write**, run each, report each exit code, and repair any check whose field names or paths do not match what the emitters actually produce, or which requires an artifact only a later stage writes. Put the repair narrative in the report body, never inside a machine-read declaration.
**Choose the terminal path by which outcome happened.** Work completed and verified writes the final verification report; anything that blocked you writes the escalation note. Write at most one.
